reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G3-NA-Q4-Harden (mat_g3_na_q4_1), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The samples directly fulfill the MATATAG competency 'Divide numbers using the 6, 7, 8, and 9 multiplication tables.' Every sample presents division problems strictly with divisors 6, 7, 8, and 9 derived from basic multiplication facts, including direct arithmetic such as "What is 48 ÷ 6?" (seed 42), "72 ÷ 8 = ___" (seed 44), "63 ÷ 7 = ___" (seed 45), and "What is 27 ÷ 9?" (seed 502). Word problems and visual array representations like "Pia wants to share 28 water bowls equally among 7 friends. How many water bowls does each friend get?" (seed 601) and "This array has 45 squares split into 9 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?" (seed 50) reinforce contextual and conceptual division based on these fact families.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample packet provides balanced and comprehensive coverage across all four required multiplication fact families: table of 6 ("What is 48 ÷ 6?", "What is 18 ÷ 6?", "What is 30 ÷ 6?", "Shade 36 squares into 6 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?"), table of 7 ("63 ÷ 7 = ___", "Ana solved: "49 ÷ 7 = ___". Ana says the missing number is 42. Is Ana correct?", "28 ÷ 7 = 4. True or False?", "What is 56 ÷ 7?", "14 ÷ 7 = ___"), table of 8 ("72 ÷ 8 = ___", "What is 64 ÷ 8?"), and table of 9 ("This array has 45 squares split into 9 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?", "Shade 72 squares into 9 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?", "81 ÷ 9 = 9. True or False?", "What is 27 ÷ 9?"). All target divisors {6, 7, 8, 9} are thoroughly exercised across various dividends.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The questions are calibrated appropriately for Grade 3 Quarter 4 learners. The language is concise and uses accessible vocabulary without extraneous complexity. Problem setups such as "Pia wants to share 28 water bowls equally among 7 friends. How many water bowls does each friend get?" (seed 601) and "Ana solved: "49 ÷ 7 = ___". Ana says the missing number is 42. Is Ana correct?" (seed 51) pose age-appropriate equal sharing scenarios and error-checking tasks that match the cognitive stage of 3rd graders without introducing extraneous arithmetic hurdles.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sample set demonstrates rich structural and formatting variety. It incorporates standard multiple choice ("What is 30 ÷ 6?", seed 46), cloze completion ("72 ÷ 8 = ___", seed 44), true/false fact verification ("28 ÷ 7 = 4. True or False?", seed 85; "81 ÷ 9 = 9. True or False?", seed 501), visual array reading ("This array has 45 squares split into 9 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?", seed 50), interactive shading tasks ("Shade 36 squares into 6 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?", seed 55; "Shade 72 squares into 9 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?", seed 500), error detection (Ana solved: "49 ÷ 7 = ___". Ana says the missing number is 42. Is Ana correct?", seed 51), and word problem application ("Pia wants to share 28 water bowls equally among 7 friends. How many water bowls does each friend get?", seed 601).

competency_alignment.rationale: Every item in the sample set aligns strictly with the target competency bounds. No items require division with remainders, multidigit long division, or division facts outside the 6, 7, 8, and 9 multiplication tables. All problems like "What is 56 ÷ 7?" (seed 600) and "What is 64 ÷ 8?" (seed 602) evaluate exact whole number division facts without introducing out-of-scope operations.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numeric range is well within the bounds of single-digit multiplication and division facts up to 9 × 9. Dividends span from 14 ("14 ÷ 7 = ___", seed 603) up to 81 ("81 ÷ 9 = 9. True or False?", seed 501), yielding single-digit whole number quotients from 2 to 9 (e.g. 18 ÷ 6 = 3, 72 ÷ 8 = 9, 49 ÷ 7 = 7, 64 ÷ 8 = 8). The scale is perfectly tailored to Grade 3 fact recall and division comprehension.
